The '''1991 FA Charity Shield''' (also known as the '''[[Wellpark Brewery|Tennent's]] FA Charity Shield''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 69th [[FA Community Shield|FA Charity Shield]], the annual football match contested by the reigning champions of the [[Football League First Division]] and the holders of the [[FA Cup]]. It was held at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]], on 10 August 1991. The game was played between [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], champions of the [[1990–91 Football League#The First Division|1990–91 Football League]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], who won the [[1990–91 FA Cup]]. This was Arsenal's twelfth Charity Shield appearance and Tottenham Hotspur's ninth.

Arsenal began the match the brighter of the two teams, dominating in possession and the number of chances created. Tottenham created their best chance to score in the first half, but struggled to find a breakthrough in the second half, hardly troubling the Arsenal defence. With neither team able to score after 90 minutes, the match ended in a draw, meaning each team would hold the trophy for six months. This was the last Shield edition to have shared winners.

==Background==
[[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] qualified for the 1991 FA Charity Shield, by virtue of winning the [[1990–91 Football League]] First Division, having lost one match&nbsp;– away to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]&nbsp;– in the entire campaign.<ref name="amb">{{cite news |title=Ambitious Arsenal aiming to deter challengers |first=John |last=Roberts |page=46 |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=10 August 1991 }}</ref> The club's previous Charity Shield appearances, eleven in total, resulted in seven wins ([[1930 FA Charity Shield|1930]], [[1931 FA Charity Shield|1931]], [[1933 FA Charity Shield|1933]], [[1934 FA Charity Shield|1934]], [[1938 FA Charity Shield|1938]], [[1948 FA Charity Shield|1948]], [[1953 FA Charity Shield|1953]]) and four losses ([[1935 FA Charity Shield|1935]], [[1936 FA Charity Shield|1936]], [[1979 FA Charity Shield|1979]], [[1989 FA Charity Shield|1989]]). [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] qualified as holders of the FA Cup, beating [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] 2–1 in the [[1991 FA Cup Final]].<ref name="amb"/> They appeared in eight previous shields, winning four outright ([[1921 FA Charity Shield|1921]], [[1951 FA Charity Shield|1951]], [[1961 FA Charity Shield|1961]], [[1962 FA Charity Shield|1962]]), sharing two ([[1967 FA Charity Shield|1967]], [[1981 FA Charity Shield|1981]]) and losing two ([[1920 FA Charity Shield|1920]], [[1982 FA Charity Shield|1982]]).

The last meeting between both teams was in the FA Cup; Tottenham Hotspur won 3–1 in the semi-final at Wembley Stadium.<ref name="pr">{{cite news |title=Arsenal aim to avenge their loss in semi-final |first=Stuart |last=Jones |page=31 |newspaper=The Times |date=10 August 1991}}</ref> Tottenham were the only league opponents to avoid defeat against Arsenal, with neither side scoring in the two matches played. Manager [[Peter Shreeves]] noted the importance of the match, given this was a [[North London derby]], but stressed there "will be more important objectives this season."<ref name="pr"/> This was the first all-London encounter in the 83-year history of the Shield.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ringing in the new with an echo of the old |first=David |last=Lacey |page=23 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=10 August 1991}}</ref> This would be the last time either team was to share the trophy, as new regulations were brought in a year later that allowed for [[extra time]] and subsequently a [[penalty shootout (association football)|penalty shootout]] if a draw occurred in normal time.<ref>{{cite news |title=Charity show gets business underway |first=David |last=Lacey |page=15 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=8 August 1992}}</ref> 

==Match==
[[Anders Limpar]] was the main absentee for Arsenal, having sustained a knee injury, on duty for the Sweden national team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fenwick in line for Spurs comeback |publisher=Agence France-Presse|date=9 August 1991}}</ref> [[David O'Leary]] started in place of the injured [[Steve Bould]]; midfielder [[David Hillier]] was selected ahead of [[Michael Thomas (footballer born 1967)|Michael Thomas]] in Limpar's place on the left wing. Tottenham defender [[Terry Fenwick]], recovered from a double leg break, replaced [[Justin Edinburgh]] in the first eleven. Without [[Paul Gascoigne]], injured in the FA Cup final, Tottenham employed a five-man midfield with [[Gary Lineker]] as the sole striker.<ref name="refe"/>

===Summary===
Arsenal began brightly in front of a crowd of 65,483,<ref name="Times"/> creating the first chance of the match in the 17th minute. [[Paul Davis (footballer born 1961)|Paul Davis]] set up striker [[Kevin Campbell (footballer)|Kevin Campbell]], who hooked the ball high over goal. Four minutes later, [[Alan Smith (footballer born 1962)|Alan Smith]] headed the ball into the goal net, meeting a cross from [[Paul Merson]]; it was ruled out by referee [[Terry Holbrook]] for offside.<ref name="report">{{cite news |title=Arsenal and Spurs share Shield |publisher=Agence France-Presse|date=10 August 1991 }}</ref> Tottenham improved shortly after, with [[Gary Mabbutt]] heading the ball directly at Arsenal goalkeeper [[David Seaman]] to create their first chance of the match. Their best opportunity to score was in the 36th minute. [[Vinny Samways]] set up Gary Lineker to break past the Arsenal defence.<ref name="refe"/> Having nudged the ball past [[Tony Adams (footballer)|Tony Adams]], Lineker looked up, before making a cross for [[Nayim]] to head; the shot was acrobatically saved by Seaman's right foot.<ref name="report"/>

Early in the second half, Tottenham's [[Pat van den Hauwe]] was cautioned by Holbrook for getting tangled with Arsenal's [[David Rocastle]], in spite Rocastle indicating that the player used an elbow&nbsp;– a bookable offence.<ref name="report"/> Moments after, Rocastle was shown a yellow card for attempting to get his own back on Van Den Hauwe, by tackling the player without intent.<ref name="report"/> Van Den Hauwe was later booked for a wild challenge on [[Lee Dixon]].<ref name="report"/> Arsenal dominated possession during the second half, with Tottenham infrequently troubling their opponent's defence and relying on counterattacks to fashion goal-scoring chances.<ref name="report"/> Smith had a chance saved in the 75th minute by goalkeeper [[Erik Thorstvedt]], when the ball was back-passed across the penalty area by [[Steve Sedgley]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Lineker left in a lonely role |first=Norman |last=Fox |page=21 |newspaper=The Independent on Sunday |location=London |date=11 August 1991}}</ref> In the final seconds of the match substitute [[Andy Cole]], who had replaced Campbell, shot from 20 yards and into the side-netting.<ref name="report"/>

==Post-match==
Despite the draw, Shreeves was content with his team's performance. He believed the new 4–5–1 formation deployed in the match was "the system which suits us best", but admitted the midfield needed to do more to support Lineker upfront.<ref name="Times"/> Arsenal manager [[George Graham (footballer, born 1944)|George Graham]] agreed that his team played below their usual standard in the first half, accepting that his team needed "to work on&nbsp;... finishing" to make use of their territorial advantage.<ref name="Times"/>
